head: 0ca9f0c6efd4de64926ea3c2fc6a22a910f5e075
summary:
At HEAD 0ca9f0c, criteria 1 to 4 hold, measured by commands run on this machine. Criterion 5 and O-006 are still not checked, because both need a second sign-in session. That makes the verdict partial, not passes.

**What changed since validate attempt 1.** The only source change since 666f197 is tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs, which adds the Fact `WindowCasesIsAscii` and a new class summary. SmbRig.cs, StallRig, StalledShareTests.cs, WindowCases.ps1, fitness.yaml and the docs are byte-for-byte as they were at attempt 1.

**The O-007 fix is in and it works.** I tested it with my own mutation, not the builder's:
- I put a right single quote (U+2019) and an é into the comment at line 1333. Both parse cases still passed under 5.1 and 7. `WindowCasesIsAscii` failed with "byte 0xE2 at offset 73286 (line 1333)".
- I prepended a UTF-8 BOM. The Fact failed with the BOM message.
- Both times the file was restored and its hash matched the original.
- I re-measured 5.1 (5.1.26100.9444) on scratch scripts: a dash or curly quotes in a comment gave 0 parse errors, and the same in a double-quoted string gave 2.

**Criteria 1 to 4, re-measured at this HEAD:**
- The full default suite passes 374/374. The 22 targeted tests pass: 18 SmbRigTests, 3 WindowScriptParseTests and 1 wording test.
- StallRig builds from its csproj outside the slnx with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Reflection on the built dll shows `RigLock.SessionName` = `Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig` as its only static field.
- **Live contention (O-005):** this shell held `Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig`. The built StallRig.exe then exited 1 after 2331 ms with a TimeoutException naming that lock. There were 0 \\127.0.0.1 mappings before and after.
- Fitness: all 59 rules hold, and the three SL-059 rules set `including_comments: true`.
- Grep finds no `MachineName` identifier in code.

**One small inaccuracy remains in the new summary.** WindowScriptParseTests.cs:9 says the parse check "covers code and string literals". But é inside a double-quoted string gave 0 parse errors under 5.1. Only characters that 5.1 decodes into quote characters break the parse. No input goes unguarded, because `WindowCasesIsAscii` checks every byte. Code review reached the same view, and I did not send the slice back over one sentence of prose.

**Why this is not a pass:**
- **O-006 (owed here):** whether one session's SMB mappings are visible to the rig's sweep in another needs a second logon session. Spike 1 showed this sandbox cannot create one, and neither registered elevated operation creates a session or reads mappings.
- **Criterion 5 (cross-session exclusion):** the design deferred it. The doc (SL-020-scanner.md:253-262) states the limit and the trigger for switching to `Global\`, but the behaviour itself is unmeasured.

**Not a loop.** build-slice ran twice. The second run was caused by the revocation over O-007, changed one test file, and closed that obligation.

criteria.criterion: 1. Rename RigLock's public scope constant, including when StallRig is built outside FsAnalyser.slnx
criteria.how: StallRig's csproj built outside the slnx at HEAD with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Reflection on the built StallRig.dll shows SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig as its only static field. No MachineName identifier is left in code. The built exe contends on the same kernel object that PowerShell opens by string.

criteria.criterion: 2. Correct the stale 'on this machine' comments, with WindowCases.ps1 still parsing under Windows PowerShell 5.1
criteria.how: All three comments now say 'in this sign-in session' or 'per sign-in session'. The WindowCasesParses cases pass under powershell.exe 5.1 and pwsh 7. WindowCases.ps1 has no BOM and 0 bytes >= 0x80. WindowCasesIsAscii now guards comments too: a mutation at line 1333 fails it while both parse cases still pass.

criteria.criterion: 3. Sweep for residual machine-wide claims about RigLock, leaving unrelated hits alone
criteria.how: The grep shows no MachineName identifier and no claim that RigLock is machine-wide. The unrelated hits were left unedited, as attempt 1 found when it read each one; those files are unchanged since. RigLockScopeWordingTests passes, and Fitness reports all 59 rules holding, with including_comments: true on the three SL-059 rules.

criteria.criterion: 4. RigLock's existing in-session serialisation, covered by the 18 existing SmbRigTests
criteria.how: All 18 SmbRigTests pass by name at HEAD, and the full suite passes 374/374. The real built StallRig.exe exits 1 after 2331 ms with a TimeoutException naming the lock while another process in session 1 holds Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig.

criteria.criterion: 5. Cross-session mutual exclusion of RigLock, when two processes in different sign-in sessions both hold a Global\ named mutex
criteria.how: The design's handling is present: there is no Global\ anywhere, and SL-020-scanner.md:253-262 states that runs from different sessions are not serialised and gives the trigger for switching. The behaviour itself was never measured, because no second session is reachable from this sandbox.

planned.evidence: StallRig's csproj built outside the slnx at 0ca9f0c with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Reflection on StallRig.dll gives SessionName = Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig. Grep finds no MachineName identifier in code. The live exe times out loudly against a held Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig.

The three comment lines are changed. WindowCasesParses passes under 5.1 and 7. The file has no BOM and is ASCII. The new WindowCasesIsAscii fails on a non-ASCII comment mutation and on a BOM mutation, and the file was restored byte-identical both times.

No residual machine-wide claim about RigLock turned up; unrelated hits were left alone. The wording test passes and Fitness reports all 59 rules holding. Attempt 1's check that Fitness fires on the parent's files stands, because those bytes are unchanged.
18/18 SmbRigTests pass by name, and the full suite passes 374/374. The real StallRig.exe exits 1 after 2331 ms with the lock named.

The design deferred this (material:false), and the doc states the limit and the trigger. Cross-session behaviour is unmeasured: spike 1 showed the sandbox cannot create a second session, and no registered elevated operation creates one.

obligations.evidence: Re-measured at HEAD. This shell held [Threading.Mutex]::new($false,'Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig') (createdNew=True). The StallRig.exe, freshly built outside the slnx, exited 1 after 2331 ms with 'Another stall-rig run held Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig for 2 s'. Reflection shows SessionName carries the unchanged string. The only code consumers are SmbRig.cs:51/:176 and the cref at SmbRigTests.cs:8.

Not measurable from this run. It needs an SMB mapping made in one logon session and Get-SmbMapping read from another. Spike 1 recorded the sandbox vetoing Register-ScheduledTask (S4U), and runas and self-elevation are forbidden. whoami and read-denied-folders neither create a session nor read mappings, so asking for either would not settle it. A person has to run it, from a second session via Fast User Switching or from an S4U task they register by hand.

WindowCasesIsAscii exists (WindowScriptParseTests.cs:18-31). My own mutation, U+2019 and é in the line-1333 comment, left both parse cases passing and failed the Fact with 'byte 0xE2 at offset 73286 (line 1333)'. A BOM mutation also failed it. The summary no longer claims the parse check catches comment characters. One residual overstatement: 'covers ... string literals', although é in a string gives 5.1 0 errors. That is prose only; the byte check covers every byte.

not_reached: O-006: whether an SMB mapping made in one sign-in session is visible to Get-SmbMapping, and so to the rig's sweep, in another. That needs a second session, which a person has to create (Fast User Switching, or an S4U task registered by hand).

Cross-session behaviour of the lock itself. The doc (SL-020-scanner.md:255-258) says Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig is never seen from another session and implies Global\ would be. Both come from recalled Microsoft semantics: spike 2's cases (a), (b) and (c) never ran.

Whether the SMB client's 'one port per server name' limit for 127.0.0.1 applies per logon session or machine-wide. If it is machine-wide, two rig runs in different sessions could still clash at the redirector even though the lock does not serialise them.

The person-run network pass at this HEAD (WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork, then Core.Tests with Network=SMB-LOOPBACK). StallRig was run only as far as the lock timeout, never through a real mapping.
A machine without pwsh.exe on PATH. The default suite now launches pwsh.exe (WindowCasesParses Core case), which is present here but not guaranteed elsewhere.
